description: Beyond Horizons is a solo project on astronaut health during long-duration missions. I built a 3D health-monitoring console that shows where in the body a problem is and links every alert to NASA limits and data. Users can monitor vitals and the habitat, simulate radiation effects on genes, follow a Mars mission, see their own risk in a crew and compare spacewalk options.
summary:
Beyond Horizons is a holographic health-monitoring console for astronauts on long missions. On one screen it tracks vital signs (heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, blood pressure, breathing), the habitat (O₂, CO₂, pressure, temperature, radiation) and long-term spaceflight risks. In Scan mode the suit becomes a 3D hologram that shows where in the body a problem is: the affected organs glow and are labelled. Every alert is checked against NASA limits and linked to its NASA source.

It goes beyond monitoring. Astronauts can log their own vitals and history, simulate how radiation changes their genes and career dose against NASA's 600 mSv limit, follow a Mars mission day by day, see their own risk inside a four-person crew, and compare options for a critical spacewalk with an auditable debate between mission roles. An AI assistant explains everything in plain language.

Far from Earth, help can be 20+ minutes away. Beyond Horizons helps a crew catch problems early, understand them, and decide with evidence.

For the best experience with the interactive 3D dashboard, use a desktop or laptop browser.
details:
What it does Beyond Horizons is a health-monitoring console for astronauts on long-duration missions, built as one mission-control screen with nine tabs:

  • Overview: live vital signs with waveforms, habitat environment against NASA-STD-3001 limits, systems status, genetic overview and AI insights. Readings turn amber (watch) or red (alert) outside their limits.
  • Astronaut mode / Scan mode: the suit turns into a translucent 3D hologram; a scan line reveals skeleton, vessels, lungs, a beating heart, digestive organs and brain. Affected systems glow and are labelled, so anyone on the crew can see in seconds where the problem is.
  • Scenarios: hypoxia, arrhythmia, solar particle event, heat stress, bone loss, SANS, plus scenarios the user creates (with a live preview and an optional mission day).
  • My Vitals: the astronaut enters their own readings; they are evaluated, saved to a history, charted, shown on the hologram and explained by the AI (value, normal range, meaning, affected organ, what to do).
  • Genetics: a radiation → gene-alteration simulator. Choose the situation (ISS, one-year mission, Mars transit), days, previous dose, a solar event and a vitamin A countermeasure, and see the dose, the career total against NASA's 600 mSv limit, the added cancer risk, which genes change (published NASA-funded data) and the consequences NASA found. The effects also appear on the astronaut's body scan.
  • Mission: follow a mission day by day; events (solar storm, exercise-machine failure, spacewalk) change the astronaut's status automatically.
  • Crew Risk: a day-by-day simulation of a four-person, 180-day Mars-transit crew in which the user takes a seat under their own name; crew traits, events and countermeasures are customizable.
  • EVA Decision: three options for a critical spacewalk after a solar storm (keep, delay, reassign) compared on success chance and risk, plus a Debate Chamber where commander, flight surgeon, science officer and a skeptic each apply one transparent formula.
  • Research: an evidence graph (14 factors, 13 links) where every link shows its evidence level and NASA source, plus a ranking of the next experiments worth doing.
  • Beyond AI: an assistant that answers questions about the crew, the scan and the user's own vitals, with care and in the user's language.

How it works A static three.js front end talks to a FastAPI back end (Render) through a Next.js proxy (Vercel). The back end runs a deterministic simulation engine, the counterfactual EVA comparison, the evidence graph and the vitals evaluation. If the server is asleep, the app keeps working on a stored snapshot of the real API outputs and says so on screen.

How the Genetics simulator works

1. Mission dose = daily dose rate × days in space (+ the solar-event dose, if chosen). Rates are NASA measurements: 0.35 mSv/day on the ISS (range 0.2–0.5, NTRS 20250006168) and 1.8 mSv/day in deep space, measured by Curiosity's RAD on the way to Mars.

2. Career total = previous missions' dose + this mission's dose, compared with NASA's career limit of 600 mSv (NASA-STD-3001). A solar event is also compared with NASA's 250 mSv per-event limit.

3. Added fatal-cancer risk ≈ 5% per sievert (1,000 mSv) of dose.

4. Dose level: under 100 mSv LOW, 100–300 MODERATE, 300–600 ELEVATED, 600+ HIGH.

5. Gene changes come from published NASA-funded data (grant NAG9-1024, irradiated rat skin): each gene's activity after radiation is compared with unirradiated controls (2× or more = up, half or less = down), with and without the vitamin A diet that the study tested. Those doses were far higher than a mission's, so the simulator shows which genes respond and in which direction, not an exact prediction for a person.

6. Biological markers (DNA damage, telomeres, gene expression, immune and oxidative stress, mitochondria) are flagged by simple, visible rules based on the dose level, mission length (180+ and 300+ days, as in the NASA Twins Study) and solar events.

7. The result also appears on the body scan: radiation lights up bone marrow and the digestive tract, and long stays in weightlessness light up bones, muscles and the brain (NASA Human Research Program).

Built-in guide (?): the "?" button in the top-right corner opens a guide to the whole app. It explains, in plain language, what each tab is for, what the colors and labels mean (SIMULATED, WATCH, ALERT, NASA source tags), how to switch between Astronaut and Scan mode, and how to customize the astronaut, the mission and the crew. Together with the A−/A+ text-size buttons, it makes the app usable by anyone, not only experts.

Benefits and impact Far from Earth, the crew cannot wait 20+ minutes for an answer from the ground. Beyond Horizons helps them detect problems earlier, understand them visually, and make decisions (for example, who should do a spacewalk) with evidence instead of guesswork. It is also a clear way to explain spaceflight health risks to students and the public.

Tools and languages JavaScript, HTML/CSS, three.js (WebGL, custom hologram shader, bloom), Python (FastAPI, Pydantic, pytest), TypeScript (Next.js, Tailwind), Jupyter notebooks, gltf-transform for 3D-model compression, Vercel and Render.

What makes it creative The suit becomes a hologram that shows where the body is in trouble; everything is connected (a solar storm in the mission changes the scan, the genetics simulator lights up the body, the user's own name appears in the crew and in the spacewalk decision); and every number is honest: simulated data is labelled SIMULATED, hypotheses are labelled as hypotheses, and every limit links to its NASA source.

Factors I considered Scientific honesty (no invented numbers, evidence levels on every link), clarity for non-experts (built-in guide, text-size controls, plain-language AI), the communication delay on deep-space missions, privacy (history stays in the user's browser) and resilience (offline snapshot). It is a research prototype, not a medical device.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI) tools:

Claude supported code development, debugging, translating and interface refinement. Project direction, feature selection and final integration remained the creator's responsibility. Beyond AI is the project's user-facing assistant, helping users understand the information presented by the platform. Simulation outputs are generated by the project's deterministic engine, not by the AI assistant.

- Beyond AI, the project's user-facing assistant, uses an Anthropic API integrated through the project's backend. It helps users understand and navigate the information presented by the platform. Simulation outputs are generated by the project's deterministic engine, not by the AI assistant.

No NASA logos or branding were used or generated.

Recommended Viewing:

For the best experience with the interactive 3D dashboard, use a desktop or laptop browser.
